rationale: Attribute the retained execution of experiment b02f82dfc4024a638ae4ecbdcb18b1fc-experiment to a grounded conclusion, and submit a corrected successor whose admission/comparison encoding matches the engine's correlation model (one shared admission event, one shared result event name, applicability selected by stale_suffix, assertions expressing the required healthy property). No source, requirement or observation is weakened: the decisive events of the retained receipt are unchanged and are cited directly.

knowledge.statement: In the retained 3-node in-memory execution, when the isolated node reconnected with its persisted log ending above the replacement leader's snapshot index (case: old_last_before=222 vs snapshot_index=45), the node's applied index stayed at the snapshot index 45 across the observation window while the leader's commit index was 55 (stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false); in the same execution the control with the node's log ending below the snapshot index (old_last_before=25) reached applied index 55 and caught up (stalled=false, isolated_caught_up=true).
knowledge.conditions: Single process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with InmemStore and FileSnapshotStore, ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, TrailingLogs=0, replacement leader compacted at or below its snapshot index; the isolated node's above-snapshot suffix was produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it stepped down.

interpretations.rationale: Decisive parsed events of the retained execution (CheckRun 61befa27ce114c8097c8bdfa597e9ee5, status completed, exit_code 0, prerequisites matched): event index 3 (case_no_progress result) reports snapshot_index=45 < old_last_before=222, old_applied_after=45, leader_commit_index=55, stalled=true, isolated_caught_up=false; event index 1 (control_catchup result) reports snapshot_index=45 > old_last_before=25, old_applied_after=55, leader_commit_index=55, stalled=false, isolated_caught_up=true. The follower therefore did not converge to the leader's log after installing the snapshot, while the same code path converged when its log did not extend above the snapshot index. This matches the producer/consumer trace: installSnapshot (raft.go:1814-1953) never truncates log entries above req.LastLogIndex and never calls setLastLog, so getLastEntry (state.go:167-174) keeps reporting the stale (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm); the AppendEntries PrevLogEntry check (raft.go:1475-1502) rejects with NoRetryBackoff, and replicateTo (replication.go:222-260) lowers nextIndex until setupAppendEntries returns ErrLogNotFound, at which point sendLatestSnapshot (replication.go:299-383) re-sends the same snapshot.

knowledge.assertion: installSnapshot does not truncate log entries above req.LastLogIndex and does not call setLastLog
getLastEntry reports the cached log index/term whenever it is at or above the snapshot index
appendEntries rejects on a missing or term-mismatched PrevLogEntry without truncating
replicateTo lowers nextIndex and falls back to re-sending the newest snapshot on ErrLogNotFound

counterevidence: The three comparisons declared in this experiment's basis evaluated as unknown, not violated: each declared prerequisite had to correlate to every result event, but the two scenario_setup admissions carry mutually exclusive scenario values, so match_prerequisites could not build one chain (observations.json comparisons[0..2] reason 'No corresponding prerequisite events reached'). This is a defect in the comparison admission encoding, not in the cited event facts.
The control event (index 1) is consistent with the ordinary snapshot install path working when the follower's log ends at or below the snapshot index, so the stall is not a blanket snapshot failure.
limitations: Single-process in-memory transport and the non-monotonic InmemStore path; network/TCP transports and MonotonicLogStore were not exercised.
Only live catch-up was observed; restart/recovery of the stalled node and any committed-entry or safety consequence were not tested.

The declared requirement text conditioned on S >= L (log at or below the snapshot index), which describes the control; the violation is observed in the opposite branch (L > S), where the follower keeps a stale suffix.
The submitted successor experiment corrects the admission/comparison encoding and needs its own receipt before it can carry an interpretation.
interpretations.report_title: 从快照恢复后保留超出快照索引的旧日志后缀导致追随者无法追上
interpretations.report_answer: 追随者安装快照时只压缩快照索引及以下的日志，既不截断索引以上的旧日志、也不更新缓存的最后日志索引/任期；因此当本机日志长于快照索引时，getLastEntry 仍返回旧的 (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm)，AppendEntries 的 PrevLogEntry 校验被拒绝，leader 逐次下调 nextIndex 直到 ErrLogNotFound 并反复重发同一快照，追随者停在快照索引不再前进（保留执行事件 1 与 3 支持该结论；对照事件显示日志未超出快照索引时可正常追上）。

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with InmemStore and FileSnapshotStore, built with the upstream MakeCluster test helper. The replacement leader compacts its log at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0) so it can no longer serve the isolated node's match point from the log store.
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's above-snapshot suffix is produced by real Apply calls on the old leader during its pre-step-down lease window; no state is injected.
The replacement leader commits post-snapshot entries with the third node so leader_commit_index rises above the snapshot index.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Monotonic log stores; the non-monotonic InmemStore path is exercised.
Restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.

experiment.prefix: Bootstrap a 3-node cluster; commit a 20-command prefix to all nodes; isolate the current leader; append 200 (case) or 2 (control) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node; let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader; commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S on the replacement leader; commit 10 post entries above S; reconnect and observe for about 4.5s; in one execution emit a scenario_setup admission event and a snapshot_catchup_result event for each of the two scenarios.
experiment.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, a persisted log suffix above S that the leader does not share must not keep the follower from accepting the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S: the follower must stop reporting a stale above-snapshot last entry and converge to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry returns the cached log index/term whenever it is at or above the snapshot index) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries rejects on a missing or term-mismatched PrevLogEntry); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 with the post-restore block at raft.go:1930-1948 is the producer responsible for establishing that state.
experiment.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop.

comparisons.description: Control (follower log at or below the snapshot index): the follower reaches the leader's commit index after snapshot catch-up.
Case (follower log extends above the snapshot index): the follower must also reach the leader's commit index; the retained run shows it does not.
Case: the follower's applied index must change across the observation window while the leader commit index is above it; the retained run shows it is frozen.

experiment.revision_reason: Corrected event and comparison encoding: the predecessor's comparisons required two mutually exclusive scenario_setup prerequisites to correlate to each result event, so all comparisons evaluated unknown. The successor emits one shared scenario_setup admission event and one shared snapshot_catchup_result event name per scenario, selects the scenario by a stale_suffix applicability condition, and asserts the required healthy property (isolated_caught_up true, stalled false) so a stalled case is a violating witness. The executed scenarios, prefix, requirement and observations are unchanged.
